Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I am Dr.

Key details

  • SV Venkatesh, Civil Engineering, Department of Science and Humanities, PS University.
  • This is class number 15.
  • In the last class, I had introduced you to the last topic of unit 1, chapter 2, that is resultant.
  • We had discussed about what is resultant, how do we find the characteristics of resultant, that is the magnitude.
  • The direction, the sense, and the point of application.
  • The point of application can be determined by using the principle of movements.
  • I had defined what is principle of moments and explained how do we find out the point of application of the resultant force for our system of forces.
  • Solve a few problems taken from the unsolved problem category from the prescribed textbook that is Engineering Mechanics Statics by Miriam Craig and Bolton published by John Wiley Publications.
  • The problem that I have chosen is 2 bar 81.
  • The statement of the problem goes something like this.
  • Replace the three horizontal forces and apply the couple with an equivalent force couple system at O.
  • By specifying the resultant R and the couple M naught, next determine the equation for the line of action of the standalone resultant force R.
  • There are three horizontal forces acting and there is a couple that is acting.
  • We have to replace this system, that is this three.
  • Forces plus one couple by an equivalent force couple system.
  • What we had earlier discussed under the topic couple, force couple system at point O.
  • Then we have a couple here.
  • Then we have to determine.
  • The line of action of the standalone resultant force.
  • Line of action of the standalone resultant force is what is the line of action of the single force where we need to apply that.
  • For any value of X and Y.
  • Where this single resultant force needs to be acting, so that we can get the same effect as that of these three forces and the couple.
  • Which is acting at this point is of magnitude 4 newton.
  • The sense of this is towards the right.
  • It is acting at a distance of 1 meter along x axis.
  • Look at the axis.
  • X axis is not the horizontal axis here, but this axis, x axis is inclined to the vertical at an angle of 70 degrees.
  • This is acting from right to left.
  • The magnitude of that is 6 kilonewtons.
  • Then we have the another force of magnitude 10 kilonewtons acting on the x-axis at this point.
  • which is equal to four meters still here.
  • Whereas this six kilometers it act is acting along the x axis at a distance of two point five meters.
  • This four kilometers is acting at a distance of one meter along the x axis.
  • That is above x axis.
  • Whereas this six kilometer is acting below x axis by a distance of 0.3 meters.
